verses.1: That night, the king’s years were counted. He ordered that the book of memories, containing the events of those days, be brought before him.
verses.2: And he found a writing that stated that Mordecai had reported about Bigthan and Tarsis, two of the king’s officers who tried to lay a hand on King Ahşverosh.
verses.3: And the king said, “What has been done to my beloved Mardochai is truly great and noble.” But the king’s servants said, “Nothing has been done to him at all.”
verses.4: And the king said, “Who is in the courtyard?” Then Hanan came into the palace courtyard. The servant said to the king, “Hang Mordecai on that tree that was prepared for him.”
verses.5: And the king’s sons said to him, “Look, the man is standing in the courtyard.” Then the king said, “Let him come forward.”
verses.6: And the man came forward. The king said to him, “What should I do with this man whom the king desires to honor?” The man replied in his heart, “Who could possibly desire more from the king than what I already have?”
verses.7: And Haman said to the king, “There is someone whom the king desires to see.”
verses.8: They will bring him a throne from which the king sits. There will also be a horse on which the king rides. And he will be given the crown of kingship upon his head.
verses.9: And he gave the oxen and the chariots into the hands of one of the officials of the Pharaohs. He dressed that man in fine clothes, as the king desired. Then he placed him on the chariot, and they rushed out of the city. They called out loudly, so that everyone would know what would happen to the man whom the king wanted.
verses.10: And the king said to Haman, “Quickly, take the food and the horse, as you have said. Do this for Mordecai the Jew who is sitting at the king’s gate. Do not say anything about what you have said.”
verses.11: And Haman took the horse and the chariot, and he set it up in the city’s square. Then he called out to him, “This will be done for the man whom the king desires to honor.”
verses.12: And Mordecai went back to the king’s gate. Haman, on the other hand, was pushed into his own house, with his head exposed.
verses.13: And Man told his wife and all his lovers everything that had happened to him. His wise men said to him, “Wife, if Mordecai, from the descendants of the Jews, were to fall before him, he would not be able to endure it, for he would surely fall before him.”
verses.14: They continued to talk with him. Then the attendants of the king arrived and rushed to bring the wine to those who were drinking it, as Esther had prepared it.
